tonight.headline: Down 22.6 before you've played, and Coker is the new worry
body: Christian Watson scored 22.6 for Footballers on Thursday night. Nobody of yours has played yet. ESPN still projects you 134.5 to their 128.6, a 53% win probability.

The bad news is your own: Jalen Coker missed Thursday's practice with his ankle after a limited Wednesday. Nothing to do today. Friday's Panthers report decides the first card below, and Friday's Steelers report decides the second.

case.label: Their lineup
case.body: Footballers start Matthew Stafford because Caleb Williams didn't practise Wednesday or Thursday (Eagles/Bears report, 24 Sep). Malik Nabers went from limited to full on Thursday (Giants.com), so he plays for them. Brock Bowers is still tagged questionable. I didn't re-check him this run.

case.label: Where the 53% comes from
case.body: It assumes Coker plays and scores 13.8. If he's out and McLaurin takes the flex, you lose about 1.9 projected points. That's still roughly a coin flip, not a collapse.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Coker ruled out and the first card not used. Then the flex scores zero and you are the underdog by about 8.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only. Friday's Panthers report, then Sunday inactives about 09:30 Mexico City. All three play at 11:00
doFirst.title: Only if Carolina rule Coker out: start McLaurin in the flex
doFirst.subtitle: Not armed. Don't do this today. The bench player it swaps in is Terry McLaurin. Nothing is dropped.

case.label: What changed
case.body: Coker was limited Wednesday and held out on Thursday with the ankle he sprained in Week 1 (Panthers.com, 24 Sep). Xavier Legette (knee) was held out too. ClutchPoints (25 Sep) called it 'a concerning turn'. On Thursday morning this brief said his availability wasn't in doubt. That's no longer true.

case.label: Why McLaurin, not Boston
case.body: McLaurin projects 11.9 and drew 9 targets in Week 2. Denzel Boston projects 11.3 and drew 7, though he's playing 93% of Cleveland's snaps with Deshaun Watson starting (Heavy, 22 Sep). That's close on both, so I'm taking the projection with no thesis. Honest cost: McLaurin gets Seattle, who've allowed the fewest WR points, with Marcus Mariota at quarterback.

case.label: No timing trap
case.body: Coker, McLaurin and Boston all kick off Sunday at 11:00 Mexico City. If Friday lists Coker questionable, wait for the inactives about 90 minutes before kickoff. The 07:00 Sunday brief runs before those, so check them yourself.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Coker practises Friday and carries no designation, or is active on Sunday. The card then never fires and costs nothing.

action.label: Start McLaurin · bench Coker (only if Coker is out)

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only. Check Friday's Steelers report; both kick off Sunday 11:00 Mexico City
doFirst.title: Only if Pittsburgh rule Warren out: start Tuten
doFirst.subtitle: Not armed, carried from yesterday. Warren starts unless Friday's report lists him OUT or DOUBTFUL. Nothing is dropped.

case.label: The evidence, now two days of it
case.body: Warren was limited Wednesday and Thursday with the shoulder. Rico Dowdle didn't practise either day with the toe (Still Curtain, 24 Sep). Limited both days isn't the pattern of a player about to be ruled out. If Warren plays, the backfield is his.

case.label: Why not now
case.body: Warren projects 15.0 to Tuten's 11.0. Swapping on a 'limited' tag throws away four points. Cincinnati have allowed the 7th-fewest RB points and New England the 9th-fewest (footballdb), so the matchups don't change it.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Warren practises fully on Friday or carries no designation. The card then never fires.

action.label: Start Tuten · bench Warren (only if Warren is out)

whatWentWrong.title: Coker missed Thursday's practice, and yesterday's brief said he was fine
whatWentWrong.lead: Limited Wednesday, held out Thursday (Panthers.com). The 13:40 UTC brief quoted a beat writer saying his availability wasn't in doubt. That's why the first card exists.

case.label: What happened
case.body: The ankle has been there since Week 1, when he had 138 yards and two scores. He played through it in Week 2 (8 for 66). Thursday is the first practice he has missed this week.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: The flex has a fallback now: McLaurin, same kickoff. Worst case is a late swap, not an empty slot.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Coker practises on Friday and plays Sunday with no designation. Then Thursday was maintenance, not a setback.

roster.footnote: Nothing of yours has played. Grades use footballdb's 2026 points-allowed table: standard scoring, two games, 1st = fewest allowed. That's a thin sample. Kicker isn't graded. Kickoffs are Mexico City time.

lineupCheck.verdict: The lineup as set is the projection lineup. The only open questions are Coker's ankle and Warren's shoulder, and both are fallback cards, not changes to make today.

starting.name: Josh Allen
starting.detail: BUF · vs LAC · SUN 11:00 · Stud, starts regardless.

starting.name: De'Von Achane
starting.detail: MIA · vs KC · SUN 11:00 · Malik Willis at QB for a winless Miami (KNBR, 24 Sep), so trailing game script is the risk. Not on Miami's report (Chiefs.com). Stud, starts regardless.

starting.name: Jaylen Warren
starting.detail: PIT · vs CIN · SUN 11:00 · QUESTIONABLE · shoulder, limited Wed and Thu. Dowdle DNP both days (Still Curtain). Second card covers him.

starting.name: Justin Jefferson
starting.detail: MIN · at TB · SUN 14:05 · Kyler Murray back as the starter (Vikings.com, Yardbarker). That's an upgrade on what he had.

starting.name: Garrett Wilson
starting.detail: NYJ · at DET · SUN 11:00 · Geno Smith throwing, not on the report. Mitchell limited (finger), TE Mason Taylor DNP Wed and Thu (NewYorkJets.com). Targets concentrate on him.

starting.name: Jalen Coker
starting.detail: CAR · at CLE · SUN 11:00 · QUESTIONABLE · ankle: limited Wed, held out Thu (Panthers.com). Bryce Young throwing. First card covers him.

starting.name: Isaiah Likely
starting.detail: NYG · vs TEN · SUN 11:00 · Jameis Winston, the backup, is now the starter for the season. Likely led the Giants with 10 targets in Week 2 (Giants.com). Nabers went full Thursday, so this game tests the route-share clause.
starting.gradeEvidence: tied 7th-10th vs TE (footballdb, standard scoring, Weeks 1-2)

starting.name: Lions D/ST
starting.detail: DET · vs NYJ · SUN 11:00 · Geno Smith not on the Jets' report. Jets without TE Mason Taylor, and Mitchell limited. The Jets' offence has given defences the 6th-fewest points (footballdb).
starting.gradeEvidence: NYJ offence 6th-fewest D/ST pts allowed (footballdb, std, 2 gms)

starting.name: Eddy Pineiro
starting.detail: SF · vs ARI · SUN 14:05 · ESPN has him K2 at 9.4. ClutchPoints have him 15th and PFN 17th. Held until the seat reopens 30 Sep.

bench.name: Bhayshul Tuten
bench.detail: JAX · vs NE · SUN 11:00 · Warren cover, same kickoff.

bench.name: Terry McLaurin
bench.detail: WSH · vs SEA · SUN 11:00 · Marcus Mariota, the backup, starting while Jayden Daniels is out with the elbow. Coker cover, same kickoff.

bench.name: Denzel Boston
bench.detail: CLE · vs CAR · SUN 11:00 · Deshaun Watson stays the starter. Boston has played 93% of snaps: 7-154-2 on 11 targets (Heavy).

bench.name: Kyle Monangai
bench.detail: CHI · vs PHI · MON 18:15 · QUESTIONABLE · knee, DNP on Chicago's estimated report (PhiladelphiaEagles.com). Case Keenum, the third-string QB, is expected to start.

bench.name: Rashod Bateman
bench.detail: BAL · vs DAL in Rio · SUN 14:25 · Lamar throwing. Zay Flowers DNP all week, and SI call it 'shocking' if he plays. Bateman had 9 targets without him in Week 2. Still behind four receivers here.

worthALook.name: Evan McPherson
worthALook.lead: The kicker comparison, answered hold again.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: Yahoo's Week 3 board (22 Sep) has McPherson K1 at Pittsburgh and Trey Smack K4. ClutchPoints (23 Sep) have Pineiro 15th, noting he didn't attempt a field goal in Week 2. ESPN still has Pineiro 9.4 above both (McPherson 7.4).

case.label: Why hold
case.body: Pineiro came in on 23 Sep. Moving him now would be the second change to that seat in a week, and every bench seat is either Coker's or Warren's cover or inside the churn window.

case.label: When to act
case.body: 30 September, when the churn window closes, if Pineiro finishes Week 3 outside the top twenty kickers while McPherson or Smack finish top five. McPherson is a free agent; Smack is on waivers here.

doNotChase.name: Dalton Schultz
doNotChase.lead: The market is right about him, and it doesn't matter here.

case.label: The role
case.body: The Houston Chronicle expect Nico Collins (hamstring) to miss again, which leaves the targets with Schultz.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Chem has one tight-end slot, and Likely holds it. The flex takes RB/WR only, so a second tight end scores you zero.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Likely showing up on a Giants injury report. He wasn't on this week's (Giants.com).

doNotChase.name: Kyle Pitts Sr.
doNotChase.lead: Penix came back on Thursday and Pitts still scored 1.5.

case.label: The fact
case.body: Atlanta won 35-14 at Green Bay. Drake London caught 9 for 194 and Bijan Robinson ran for 194 (FOX box score). Pitts managed 1.5 PPR. PFF: two catches in three games.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: One tight-end slot, held by Likely. The flex is RB/WR only.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Likely getting hurt. Separately, the log grades the decline WRONG if Pitts outscores Likely in two of the next three weeks. He's 0 for 1 on that so far, pending Sunday.

doNotChase.name: Jaxson Dart
doNotChase.lead: Still a big ownership anomaly, and falling for a reason.

case.label: The fact
case.body: Giants.com (24 Sep) calls the knee injury season-ending, and Winston is the starter.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing. You start Josh Allen in a one-quarterback league.

waiverAnalysis.summary: Nothing on the wire beats this roster on usage (Monangai at RB and Boston at WR are the weakest movable, and nothing clears either). Two weeks of data is a thin sample, but the tool's answer stands and I didn't go looking for a reason to disagree.

settled.title: 'Coker's availability isn't in doubt' (24 Sep, 13:40Z)
settled.result: Contradicted on Thursday: he was held out of practice (Panthers.com). It hasn't cost anything yet, and the first card is the fix.

settled.title: Let Kyle Pitts go; Chem can't use a second tight end (23 Sep)
settled.result: Penix returned on Thursday, and Pitts scored 1.5 in a 35-14 win. The quarterback risk was never the reason.

settled.title: Publish the Bateman add as a fallback card (23 Sep, 13:05Z)
settled.result: Used within ninety minutes, and it took the Vikings D/ST with it. It's the reason every fallback card now starts with 'Only if'.

settled.title: Hold Isaiah Likely through the Giants' quarterback change (22 Sep)
settled.result: Dart is out for the season, Winston is the starter, and Likely leads the team in targets (Giants.com). The target clause is graded after Sunday.
